data.description:
# The defect

`infra/scripts/observability.sh` reads its Docker and journald budgets by executing two cap
scripts as siblings of the running probe:

```
458: DOCKER_CAP_SH="${DOCKER_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/docker-storage-cap.sh}"
925: JOURNALD_CAP_SH="${JOURNALD_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/journald-cap.sh}"
```

The probe is installed at `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh`
(`install-observability.sh:12`), so these resolve to `/usr/local/bin/docker-storage-cap.sh` and
`/usr/local/bin/journald-cap.sh`.

**No path in the repository ever writes those two files.** `install-observability.sh` installs
only `observability.sh`. Unlike `vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`, neither of these two
scripts defines an `INSTALLED_PATH`, so neither self-installs; `compose-up.sh:69,84` invokes
`--install` on each, but from `${SCRIPT_DIR}` — the checkout — which configures Docker/journald
without placing the script at the probe's sibling path.

Both files are nonetheless present on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, dated `Sep 5 01:05`, which is a
manual operator copy: it matches no automated step, and the two share a timestamp distinct from
the probe's (`Sep 6 00:42`).

## Why this matters

`docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` and `journal_used_percent`
publish today ONLY because of that manual copy. Any host rebuild, AMI replacement, or
`/usr/local/bin` cleanup silently takes all three cap-compliance percentages off the air — and
the failure is silent in the specific way that matters: `pct_of_cap` is simply never reached,
so there is no error, no `probe_truncated`, and no metric. The mechanism is proven on the same
host by its two siblings, `vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`, which are ABSENT from
`/usr/local/bin` and whose percentages are correspondingly absent from the `rebar/host`
namespace (bug `exorable-gemstone-bluefish`, `1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`).

This ticket is the surviving half of that defect: the same coupling, currently satisfied by an
artifact no repository path reproduces.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A repository path installs `docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh` to the location the
   probe resolves, so a host built only from repository steps has them present. It runs on the
   same trigger that refreshes the probe, so the scripts and the probe that executes them
   cannot drift apart.
2. The trigger set that re-materializes the probe covers the cap scripts, so a change to a cap
   script reaches the box. Today `autodeploy.sh:259` sets
   `OBS_PATHS='infra/scripts/observability.sh infra/scripts/install-observability.sh'`, and a
   cap-script-only change matches no trigger and reaches no host.
3. Installation is idempotent and non-fatal on failure, matching the existing
   `install-observability.sh` and `compose-up.sh` cap-install conventions, so a cap-install
   failure cannot roll back the probe or refuse a boot.
4. A test proves a probe installed by repository steps alone can execute every cap script it
   references — i.e. for each `*_CAP_SH` default in `observability.sh`, the installer places a
   file at that path. Removing an install step fails that test.
5. `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the affected `tests/scripts/` suites pass.

## Evidence

```
$ ls -la /usr/local/bin/ | grep -iE 'rebar|cap'
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root  17285 Sep  5 01:05 docker-storage-cap.sh
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root  14603 Sep  5 01:05 journald-cap.sh
-rwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 118730 Sep  6 00:42 rebar-observability.sh
```

No `vartmp-cap.sh`, no `container-cap.sh`, and no `rebar-`-prefixed cap script of any kind.
data.title: Two cap scripts the probe depends on reached /usr/local/bin only by manual operator copy — no repo path installs them, so the working half of the cap observability is one host rebuild from silence
